### Start local docs development server

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

Starts the local development server for the documentation workspace (@zod/docs).

```sh
nub run --filter=@zod/docs dev
```

### Install zod and @zod/mini with npm

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/mini/README.md

Install @zod/mini alongside its peer dependency zod using npm.

```sh
npm install zod @zod/mini
```

### Install Nub v0.8.3

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

Installs Nub version 0.8.3, which manages dependencies, scripts, and Node versions. Restart the shell after installation so Nub is added to PATH.

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nubjs/nub/0ae8783f1f93763c56dfc827892cfb679e8a0a77/install.sh | bash -s -- 0.8.3
```

### Install external parser using z.withParser()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/blog/zod-4-6.mdx

Applies an externally generated parser or type guard to a schema to avoid new Function execution under strict Content Security Policies. The parser must return the processed schema output or return z.INVALID to delegate error handling to Zod.

```typescript
const Player = z.object({ username: z.string(), xp: z.number() });

// isPlayer is a type guard your build step generated
const Fast = z.withParser(Player, (input) =>
  isPlayer(input) ? { username: input.username, xp: input.xp } : z.INVALID
);
```

--------------------------------

### Inspect materialized schema metadata properties on first read

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/blog/zod-4-6.mdx

Shows how metadata keys like .minLength start as prototype getters and materialize as own properties only after they are read.

```ts
const s = z.string().min(3).max(9);

Object.keys(s); // 4.5: ["def", "type", "format", "minLength", "maxLength"] — 4.6: ["def", "type"]
s.minLength;    // 3 in both
Object.keys(s); // 4.6: ["def", "type", "minLength"]
```

### Build docs for production

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

Sets the required GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable and runs the production build for @zod/docs. The token is used to fetch repository stargazer counts.

```sh
export GITHUB_TOKEN=your_token_here # persists in shell session
nub run --filter=@zod/docs build
```

### Push initial branch with explicit refspec and verify output

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/AGENTS.md

Use an explicit refspec on the initial push to ensure the remote ref targets a new branch instead of main. Verify that the output displays a new branch creation rather than pointing to main.

```bash
# Always use a refspec on the initial push so the remote ref name is unambiguous.
git push -u origin <branch>:refs/heads/<branch>
```

```text
* [new branch]      <branch> -> <branch>
```

### Enable default compilation in entrypoint

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/blog/introducing-z-compile.mdx

Import `zod/compile` in your entrypoint or before defining schemas to enable compile-by-default.

```ts
// in your entrypoint (or before any schemas are defined)
import "zod/compile";
```

### z.uuid(params?)

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Validates RFC 9562/4122 compliant UUID strings with optional version constraints. Convenience methods and relaxed GUID validation are also available.

```APIDOC
### Function
`z.uuid(params?: { version?: "v1" | "v2" | "v3" | "v4" | "v5" | "v6" | "v7" | "v8" })`

### Description
Creates a schema to validate UUID strings. Supports filtering by UUID version or using convenience helpers such as `z.uuidv4()`, `z.uuidv6()`, and `z.uuidv7()`. Use `z.guid()` to validate UUID-like identifiers without RFC byte constraints.

### Parameters
- `params` (object, optional)
  - `version` (string, optional) - Specifies the UUID version: `"v1"`, `"v2"`, `"v3"`, `"v4"`, `"v5"`, `"v6"`, `"v7"`, or `"v8"`.

### Returns
A Zod schema instance for validating UUID strings.

### Usage Example
```ts
z.uuid();
z.uuid({ version: "v4" });

// Convenience helpers
z.uuidv4();
z.uuidv6();
z.uuidv7();

// Relaxed UUID-like identifier
z.guid();
```
```

--------------------------------

### Project schema input and output with z.input() and z.output()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/blog/zod-4-5.mdx

Projects a schema onto either its input or output side to validate codec halves independently. This behaves as a no-op on schemas without codecs or pipes.

```ts
const isoDate = z.codec(z.iso.datetime(), z.date(), {
  decode: (s) => new Date(s),
  encode: (d) => d.toISOString(),
});

const Event = z.object({ name: z.string(), at: isoDate });

z.input(Event).parse({ name: "launch", at: "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" }); // ✅
z.output(Event).parse({ name: "launch", at: new Date() });            // ✅
```

--------------------------------

### Configure peerDependencies to support Zod 3 and Zod 4

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/library-authors.mdx

Widen your package.json peer dependency to span both Zod 3 and Zod 4 ranges. The zod/v4 subpath is available starting in version 3.25.0.

```json
// package.json
{
  // ...
  "peerDependencies": {
    "zod": "^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0"
  }
}
```

### Enable zod/compile via Node.js CLI flags

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/blog/introducing-z-compile.mdx

Preload `zod/compile` using Node CLI arguments to guarantee it runs before any module defines a schema in ESM or CommonJS.

```sh
node --import zod/compile app.js   # ESM
node --require zod/compile app.cjs # CommonJS
```

### Preload zod/compile in nub.jsonc

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/blog/introducing-z-compile.mdx

Configure `preload` in configuration files like `nub.jsonc` or `bunfig.toml` to automatically load `zod/compile`.

```jsonc
{
  "preload": ["zod/compile"]
}
```

### Define and parse schemas using @zod/mini

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/mini/README.md

Import @zod/mini to define an object schema with checks and parse input data.

```ts
import * as z from "@zod/mini";

const User = z.object({
  name: z.string(),
  age: z.number().check(z.int(), z.positive()),
});

z.parse(User, { name: "Colin", age: 30 });
```

--------------------------------

### Use async and safe variants of decode

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/codecs.mdx

Demonstrates the return types of synchronous, asynchronous, and safe execution variants for decoding.

```ts
stringToDate.decode("2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z"); 
// => Date

stringToDate.decodeAsync("2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z"); 
// => Promise<Date>

stringToDate.safeDecode("2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z"); 
// => { success: true, data: Date } | { success: false, error: ZodError }

stringToDate.safeDecodeAsync("2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z"); 
// => Promise<{ success: true, data: Date } | { success: false, error: ZodError }>
```

Initialize a custom registry typed with specific metadata attributes.

```ts
import * as z from "zod";

const myRegistry = z.registry<{ description: string };>();
```

### Register schema using .register() method

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/metadata.mdx

Adds a schema to a registry using the schema's `.register()` method, which returns the original schema instance rather than a copy.

```ts
const mySchema = z.string();

mySchema.register(myRegistry, { description: "A cool schema!" });
// => mySchema
```

--------------------------------

### Compare prefault and default with mutating refinements

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Shows that `.prefault()` passes the fallback through mutating refinements (such as trim and toUpperCase), whereas `.default()` returns the default value without mutating it.

```ts
const a = z.string().trim().toUpperCase().prefault("  tuna  ");
a.parse(undefined); // => "TUNA"

const b = z.string().trim().toUpperCase().default("  tuna  ");
b.parse(undefined); // => "  tuna  "
```

--------------------------------

### Define a bidirectional transformation codec with z.codec()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/codecs.mdx

Create a codec by supplying an input schema, output schema, and explicit decode/encode transform functions.

```ts
const stringToDate = z.codec(
  z.iso.datetime(),  // input schema: ISO date string
  z.date(),          // output schema: Date object
  {
    decode: (isoString) => new Date(isoString), // ISO string → Date
    encode: (date) => date.toISOString(),       // Date → ISO string
  }
);
```

Preloads zod/compile via the Node.js CLI to ensure compilation is enabled before any module defines a schema.

```sh
node --import zod/compile app.js
```

### Define base recipe object schema

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Defines an initial object schema with required, optional, and array fields used for demonstrating pick, omit, and partial operations.

```ts
const Recipe = z.object({
  title: z.string(),
  description: z.string().optional(),
  ingredients: z.array(z.string()),
});
// { title: string; description?: string | undefined; ingredients: string[] }
```

### Validate unknown keys with .catchall()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Applies a catchall schema to validate any unrecognized keys present in the input.

```ts
const DogWithStrings = z
  .object({
    name: z.string(),
    age: z.number().optional(),
  })
  .catchall(z.string());


DogWithStrings.parse({ name: "Yeller", extraKey: "extraValue" }); // ✅
DogWithStrings.parse({ name: "Yeller", extraKey: 42 }); // ❌
```

```ts
const DogWithStrings = z.catchall(
  z.object({
    name: z.string(),
    age: z.number().optional(),
  }),
  z.string()
);

DogWithStrings.parse({ name: "Yeller", extraKey: "extraValue" }); // ✅
DogWithStrings.parse({ name: "Yeller", extraKey: 42 }); // ❌
```

--------------------------------

### Return output directly using default short-circuiting

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Demonstrates how `.default()` short-circuits the parsing process on undefined input, requiring a value assignable to the output type.

```ts
const schema = z.string().transform(val => val.length).default(0);
schema.parse(undefined); // => 0
```

### Invoke standard ZodType instance methods

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/packages/zod.mdx

Demonstrates parsing, refinement, wrapper, metadata, and utility methods available on all ZodType instances.

```typescript
import * as z from "zod";

const mySchema = z.string();

// parsing
mySchema.parse(data);
mySchema.safeParse(data);
mySchema.parseAsync(data);
mySchema.safeParseAsync(data);


// refinements
mySchema.refine(refinementFunc);
mySchema.superRefine(refinementFunc); // deprecated, use `.check()`
mySchema.overwrite(overwriteFunc);

// wrappers
mySchema.optional();
mySchema.nonoptional();
mySchema.nullable();
mySchema.nullish();
mySchema.default(defaultValue);
mySchema.array();
mySchema.or(otherSchema);
mySchema.transform(transformFunc);
mySchema.catch(catchValue);
mySchema.pipe(otherSchema);
mySchema.readonly();

// metadata and registries
mySchema.register(registry, metadata);
mySchema.describe(description);
mySchema.meta(metadata);

// utilities
mySchema.check(checkOrFunction);
mySchema.clone(def);
mySchema.brand<T>();
mySchema.isOptional(); // boolean
mySchema.isNullable(); // boolean
```

### Handle multiple matching options error in z.xor()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Shows how z.xor() fails with an error when the input matches more than one option schema.

```ts
const overlapping = z.xor([z.string(), z.any()]);
overlapping.parse("hello"); // ❌ fails (matches both string and any)
// ZodError: Invalid input: more than one option matched
```

### Handling Absent Keys and Optionality in Zod

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/wiki/optionality.md

Demonstrates runtime parsing and static typing behavior for transforms, coerce/unknown schemas, exactOptional modifiers, and preprocess pipes when keys are absent or undefined.

```typescript
z.object({ a: z.unknown().transform((v) => String(v ?? "X")).pipe(z.string()) }).parse({})
// → THROW  (outer pipe.optin = inner pipe.optin = unknown.optin = undefined — transform is
//   on the OUT side of the inner pipe, which is on the IN side of the outer pipe; the leading
//   `z.unknown()` drives optin and it's not "optional")
//
//   Compare to z.preprocess(fn, T):
//     z.preprocess(fn, T) === pipe(transform(fn), T)         — transform IS def.in of the only pipe
//     z.unknown().transform(fn).pipe(T) === pipe(pipe(unknown, transform), T)  — there's an
//                                                                                inner pipe with
//                                                                                z.unknown() on
//                                                                                the in side
//
//   Preprocess accepts absent because its leading position is the transform itself.
//   The unknown.transform.pipe(T) shape doesn't, because its leading position is z.unknown().
//   If you want preprocess-like absence-handling, use z.preprocess; if you specifically want
//   strict input typing on the leading slot, the unknown.transform.pipe shape gives that.

// === Coerce / unknown / any (intentionally strict on absent) ===

z.object({ a: z.coerce.string() }).parse({})
// → THROW  (coerce.string.optin = undefined; object rejects absent key)

z.object({ a: z.unknown() }).parse({})
// → THROW  (unknown.optin = undefined; soundness fix from 4.4)

z.object({ a: z.any() }).parse({})
// → THROW  (same)

// === exactOptional (delegates instead of short-circuiting) ===

z.object({ a: z.coerce.string().exactOptional() }).parse({})
// → {}  (absent + middle rung: the object drops what coerce made of undefined)

z.object({ a: z.coerce.string().exactOptional() }).parse({ a: undefined })
// → { a: "undefined" }  (present: the inner runs and its answer stands)

z.object({ a: z.string().exactOptional() }).parse({ a: undefined })
// → THROW  (present: string rejects undefined, and the object surfaces it)

z.object({ a: z.string().default("x").exactOptional() }).parse({})
// → { a: "x" }  (top rung substitutes, so the gate doesn't fire)

z.tuple([z.string(), z.coerce.string().exactOptional()]).parse(["x"])
// → ["x"]  (the tuple analog: truncate rather than materialize)

// === Static type vs runtime divergence ===

z.input<typeof z.object({ a: z.string().catch("c") })>
// → { a: string }   — `a` is required at the type level

z.object({ a: z.string().catch("c") }).parse({})
// → { a: "c" }      — but accepts {} at runtime

z.input<typeof z.object({ a: z.preprocess(fn, T) })>
// → { a: <transform's input type> }   — `a` is required at the type level

z.object({ a: z.preprocess(fn, T) }).parse({})
// → { a: fn(undefined) }   — accepts {} at runtime
```

--------------------------------

### Extract runtime input and output schemas with z.input() and z.output()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Replaces every pipe in a schema with its input or output side, reaching nested codecs inside objects, records, or maps where .in/.out cannot.

```ts
const Event = z.object({ name: z.string(), at: stringToDate });

z.input(Event).parse({ name: "launch", at: "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" }); // ✅
z.output(Event).parse({ name: "launch", at: new Date() });            // ✅
```

### z.file()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Creates a schema to validate File instances. Supports constraints on file size and MIME types using chaining or helper checks.

```APIDOC
### Method
`z.file()`

### Description
Defines a schema for validating `File` instances with optional size limits and MIME type rules.

### Chained Methods (Zod)
- **.min(size: number)**: Enforces a minimum file size in bytes.
- **.max(size: number)**: Enforces a maximum file size in bytes.
- **.mime(mimeType: string | string[])**: Enforces valid MIME type(s).

### Checks (Zod Mini)
- **z.minSize(size: number)**: Check for minimum file size in bytes.
- **z.maxSize(size: number)**: Check for maximum file size in bytes.
- **z.mime(mimeType: string | string[])**: Check for MIME type(s).

### Usage Example
```ts
// Standard Zod
const fileSchema = z.file();
fileSchema.min(10_000);
fileSchema.max(1_000_000);
fileSchema.mime("image/png");
fileSchema.mime(["image/png", "image/jpeg"]);

// Zod Mini
const fileSchemaMini = z.file();
fileSchemaMini.check(z.minSize(10_000));
fileSchemaMini.check(z.maxSize(1_000_000));
fileSchemaMini.check(z.mime("image/png"));
fileSchemaMini.check(z.mime(["image/png", "image/jpeg"]));
```
```

### z.mac(options?)

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Creates a Zod schema validating standard 48-bit IEEE 802 MAC address strings with support for custom delimiters.

```APIDOC
### Function
`z.mac(options?)`

### Description
Validates standard 48-bit IEEE 802 MAC addresses. Defaults to colon-delimited uppercase formatting.

### Parameters
- **options** (object, optional)
  - **delimiter** (string, optional) - Custom separator character (e.g., `"-"`).

### Usage Example
```ts
const mac = z.mac();
mac.parse("00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E"); // Valid

const dashMac = z.mac({ delimiter: "-" });
dashMac.parse("00-1A-2B-3C-4D-5E"); // Valid
```
```

--------------------------------

### Simulate nominal typing with .brand()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Simulate nominal typing by attaching unique brand tags to schemas so structurally identical types cannot be assigned to one another. Data must be parsed through the schema to acquire the branded type.

```typescript
const Cat = z.object({ name: z.string() }).brand<"Cat">();
const Dog = z.object({ name: z.string() }).brand<"Dog">();

type Cat = z.infer<typeof Cat>; // { name: string } & z.$brand<"Cat">
type Dog = z.infer<typeof Dog>; // { name: string } & z.$brand<"Dog">

const pluto = Dog.parse({ name: "pluto" });
const simba: Cat = pluto; // ❌ not allowed
```

--------------------------------

### Normalize URL with new URL()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Shows how new URL() normalizes URLs by resolving paths, lowercasing schemes and hosts, and escaping special characters.

```ts
new URL("HTTP://ExAmPle.com:80/./a/../b?X=1#f oo").href
// => "http://example.com/b?X=1#f%20oo"
```

--------------------------------

### Register metadata with .meta() or z.globalRegistry

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/json-schema.mdx

Registers metadata fields such as title and description on a Zod schema to include them in the generated JSON Schema.

```ts
import * as z from "zod";

// `.meta()` is a convenience method for registering a schema in `z.globalRegistry`
const emailSchema = z.string().meta({ 
  title: "Email address",
  description: "Your email address",
});

z.toJSONSchema(emailSchema);
// => { type: "string", title: "Email address", description: "Your email address", ... } 
```

```ts
import * as z from "zod";

// `.meta()` is a convenience method for registering a schema in `z.globalRegistry`
const emailSchema = z.string().register(z.globalRegistry, { 
  title: "Email address",
  description: "Your email address",
});

z.toJSONSchema(emailSchema);
// => { type: "string", title: "Email address", description: "Your email address", ... } 
```

--------------------------------

### .pick()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Selects specified keys from an existing object schema, returning a new schema with only those keys.

```APIDOC
## `.pick(mask)` / `z.pick(schema, mask)`

### Description
Creates a new object schema by picking specific keys from the base schema.

### Usage
```ts
// Zod
schema.pick({ [key]: true });

// Zod Mini
z.pick(schema, { [key]: true });
```

### Parameters
- **mask** (object) - Required - An object with keys set to `true` representing fields to pick from the schema.

### Example
```ts
const Recipe = z.object({
  title: z.string(),
  description: z.string().optional(),
  ingredients: z.array(z.string()),
});

const JustTheTitle = Recipe.pick({ title: true });
```
```

--------------------------------

### Pick keys using pick API

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Extracts specific keys from an object schema using .pick() in Zod or z.pick() in Zod Mini.

```ts
const JustTheTitle = Recipe.pick({ title: true });
```

```ts
const JustTheTitle = z.pick(Recipe, { title: true });
```

Demonstrates how `.prefault()` parses a fallback value through transformations instead of short-circuiting, requiring an input-type assignable value.

```ts
const schema = z.string().transform(val => val.length).prefault("tuna");
schema.parse(undefined); // => 4

### import "zod/compile"

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/compile.mdx

Enables compilation globally for an application. Every schema constructed after this import is compiled automatically the first time it parses.

```APIDOC
### Module Import
`import "zod/compile"`

### Description
Enables schema compilation globally. Every schema constructed after this import is compiled lazily on first parse. Designed for application use rather than libraries.

### Usage Examples
```ts
import "zod/compile"; // must come before modules that define schemas
import * as z from "zod";

const schema = z.object({ name: z.string() });
schema.parse({ name: "ok" }); // compiled on first parse
```

CLI invocation:
```sh
node --import zod/compile app.js   # ESM
node --require zod/compile app.cjs # CommonJS
```
```

### Importing base classes and utilities from zod/v4/core

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/packages/core.mdx

Exports core schema classes, parser subclasses, check definitions, error base classes, and utility functions. This package is designed to be extended rather than used directly.

```ts
import * as z from "zod/v4/core";

// the base class for all Zod schemas
z.$ZodType;

// subclasses of $ZodType that implement common parsers
z.$ZodString
z.$ZodObject
z.$ZodArray
// ...

// the base class for all Zod checks
z.$ZodCheck;

// subclasses of $ZodCheck that implement common checks
z.$ZodCheckMinLength
z.$ZodCheckMaxLength

// the base class for all Zod errors
z.$ZodError;

// issue formats (types only)
{} as z.$ZodIssue;

// utils
z.util.isValidJWT(...);
```

### z.iso.datetime(options?)

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Creates a Zod schema validating ISO 8601 datetime strings with configurable options for timezone offsets, unqualified local datetimes, and decimal precision.

```APIDOC
### Function
`z.iso.datetime(options?)`

### Description
Validates ISO 8601 datetime strings using regular expressions. By default, requires UTC format with `Z` suffix, disallows timezone offsets, requires seconds, and permits arbitrary sub-second precision.

### Parameters
- **options** (object, optional)
  - **offset** (boolean, optional) - When `true`, allows explicit timezone offsets (e.g., `+02:00`).
  - **local** (boolean, optional) - When `true`, allows timezone-less datetimes and optional seconds.
  - **precision** (number, optional) - Constrains fractional second precision. Pass `-1` for minute precision (no seconds), `0` for whole seconds, or `3` for millisecond precision.

### Usage Example
```ts
// Default (UTC only with Z)
const datetime = z.iso.datetime();
datetime.parse("2020-01-01T06:15:00Z"); // Valid

// With timezone offset
const withOffset = z.iso.datetime({ offset: true });
withOffset.parse("2020-01-01T06:15:00+02:00"); // Valid

// Local datetime
const localDt = z.iso.datetime({ local: true });
localDt.parse("2020-01-01T06:15"); // Valid

// Specific precision (milliseconds)
const millis = z.iso.datetime({ precision: 3 });
millis.parse("2020-01-01T06:15:00.123Z"); // Valid
```
```

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/blog/zod-4-6.mdx

Parses an instance with okResponse to return the untouched input object reference. The prototype survives and methods remain accessible.

```ts
const res = await fetch("/api/user");

okResponse.parse(res) === res; // ✅ true
```

### Evaluate optionality interactions with catch, default, prefault, preprocess, and transform

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/wiki/optionality.md

Details the evaluation results and optin mechanics for schema combinations using catch, default, prefault, preprocess, transform, and optional modifiers. Illustrates how different modifiers resolve undefined inputs, transform pipelines, and object property omission.

```typescript
// === Catch ===

z.string().catch("c").parse(undefined)
// → "c"  (catch fires on string(undefined) failure; nothing outer to override it)

z.string().catch("c").parse(123)
// → "c"  (catch fires on string(123) failure)

z.string().catch("c").optional().parse(undefined)
// → undefined  (catch.optin = "optional", not "defaulted", so optional yields undefined without running it)

z.string().catch("c").optional().parse("hi")
// → "hi"  (input defined, so optional just runs the inner)

z.string().catch("c").transform((s) => s + "!").optional().parse(undefined)
// → undefined  (pipe.optin = catch.optin = "optional"; optional yields undefined)

z.object({ a: z.string().catch("c") }).parse({})
// → { a: "c" }  (catch.optin = "optional" runtime; obj invokes catch with undefined; catch fires)

z.object({ a: z.string().catch("c") }).parse({ a: undefined })
// → { a: "c" }  (key present with undefined; catch fires on string(undefined))

z.object({ a: z.string().catch("c").optional() }).parse({})
// → {}  (key absent; optional sees optin = "optional", not "defaulted", so yields undefined; obj omits)

// === Default ===

z.string().default("d").parse(undefined)
// → "d"  (default short-circuits on undef input, returns d directly)

z.string().default("d").optional().parse(undefined)
// → "d"  (default.optin = "defaulted"; optional runs it and respects the result)

z.object({ a: z.string().default("d") }).parse({})
// → { a: "d" }  (obj asks optin !== undefined; invokes default; short-circuits to d)

// === Prefault ===

z.string().prefault("p").parse(undefined)
// → "p"  (prefault substitutes, runs inner string("p") which succeeds)

z.string().prefault("p").optional().parse(undefined)
// → "p"  (prefault.optin = "defaulted" — it answers the absence, so optional respects it)

// === Preprocess ===

z.preprocess((v) => v ?? "X", z.string()).parse(undefined)
// → "X"  (preprocess fn produces "X", inner string accepts)

z.preprocess((v) => v ?? "X", z.string()).optional().parse(undefined)
// → undefined  (pipe.optin = transform.optin = "optional"; optional yields undefined, fn never runs)

z.object({ a: z.preprocess((v) => v ?? "X", z.string()) }).parse({})
// → { a: "X" }  (preprocess.optin = "optional" via transform; obj invokes; fn runs)

z.object({ a: z.preprocess((v) => v ?? "X", z.string()).optional() }).parse({})
// → {}  (optional sees "optional", not "defaulted"; yields undefined without running the fn; obj omits)

z.object({ a: z.preprocess((v) => v, z.string().optional()) }).parse({})
// → {}  (inner-optional preprocess; #5917/#5929 path)

// === Default feeding a transform (the #6321 shape) ===

z.string().default("").transform((v) => (v ? v.split(",") : [])).optional().parse(undefined)
// → []  (pipe.optin = def.in.optin = default.optin = "defaulted"; optional runs it and respects)
//   4.4.3-4.4.x: was undefined, because transform flagged every invocation as a fallback

z.object({ a: z.string().default("").transform((v) => v.length) }).partial().parse({})
// → { a: 0 }  (.partial() wraps in optional; the top rung carries through the pipe)

// === Transform ===

z.string().transform((s) => s + "!").parse("hi")
// → "hi!"

z.string().transform((s) => s + "!").parse(undefined)
// → THROW  (string rejects undef before transform runs)

z.transform((v) => v ?? "X").parse(undefined)
// → "X"  (transform fn runs on undef, returns "X")

z.transform((v) => v ?? "X").optional().parse(undefined)
// → undefined  (transform.optin = "optional"; optional yields undefined, fn never runs)

z.object({ a: z.transform((v) => v ?? "X") }).parse({})
// → { a: "X" }  (transform.optin = "optional" runtime; obj invokes transform with undef)

z.object({ a: z.string().transform((s) => s + "!") }).parse({})
// → THROW  (pipe.optin = string.optin = undefined — transform on OUT side doesn't drive optin)
```

### z.function()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Utility for defining schemas for functions with input and output validation. Provides .implement() and .implementAsync() methods.

```APIDOC
## z.function(schemaDefinition)

### Description
Defines a Zod-validated function schema, separating validation logic from business logic. Throws a `ZodError` if inputs or outputs fail validation.

### Signature
```ts
z.function({
  input?: ZodTypeAny[] | ZodTuple,
  output?: ZodTypeAny
})
```

### Parameters
- **input** (`ZodTypeAny[] | ZodTuple`, optional) - Array or ZodTuple defining parameter validation schemas.
- **output** (`ZodTypeAny`, optional) - Schema defining the return type validation.

### Methods

#### `.implement(fn)`
Accepts a synchronous function implementation and returns a wrapped function that validates arguments and return values.

```ts
const MyFunction = z.function({
  input: [z.string()],
  output: z.number()
});

const computeTrimmedLength = MyFunction.implement((input) => {
  return input.trim().length;
});
```

#### `.implementAsync(fn)`
Accepts an asynchronous function implementation and returns a wrapped async function that validates arguments and return values.

```ts
const computeTrimmedLengthAsync = MyFunction.implementAsync(
  async (input) => input.trim().length
);
```
```

Provide a configuration object as the second argument to `z.toJSONSchema()` to customize the conversion behavior.

```typescript
z.toJSONSchema(schema, {
  // ...params
})

### Convert file schema with size and MIME constraints

z.file().min(1).max(1024 * 1024).mime("image/png");
// => {
//   type: "string",
//   format: "binary",
//   contentEncoding: "binary",
//   contentMediaType: "image/png",
//   minLength: 1,
//   maxLength: 1048576,
// }
```

### Inspect customized issue path with safeParse

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Executes safeParse on the schema to demonstrate the custom path set in the resulting error issue.

```typescript
const result = passwordForm.safeParse({ password: "asdf", confirm: "qwer" });
result.error.issues;
/* [{
  "code": "custom",
  "path": [ "confirm" ],
  "message": "Passwords don't match"
}] */
```

```typescript
const result = z.safeParse(passwordForm, { password: "asdf", confirm: "qwer" });
result.error.issues;

  "code": "custom",
  "path": [ "confirm" ],
  "message": "Passwords don't match"
}] */

### Inspect default input and output types for branded schemas

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

By default, `.brand()` only brands the output type (`z.output`), leaving the input type (`z.input`) unbranded.

```typescript
const USD = z.string().brand<"USD">();

type USDOutput = z.output<typeof USD>; // string & z.$brand<"USD">
type USDInput = z.input<typeof USD>; // string
```

--------------------------------

### Parse, decode, and encode with standard Zod schema methods

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/codecs.mdx

Execute forward parsing and decoding or backward encoding on standard Zod schemas where input and output types match.

```ts
const schema = z.string();

type Input = z.input<typeof schema>;    // string
type Output = z.output<typeof schema>;  // string

schema.parse("asdf");   // => "asdf"
schema.decode("asdf");  // => "asdf"
schema.encode("asdf");  // => "asdf"
```

### Chain schemas into pipes with pipe

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Chains schemas together to parse and transform values sequentially. Shown in both standard Zod and Zod Mini syntax.

```ts
const stringToLength = z.string().pipe(z.transform(val => val.length));

stringToLength.parse("hello"); // => 5
```

```ts
const stringToLength = z.pipe(z.string(), z.transform(val => val.length));

z.parse(stringToLength, "hello"); // => 5
```

### z.iso.time(options?)

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Creates a Zod schema validating time strings in the format HH:MM[:SS[.s+]] with configurable decimal precision.

```APIDOC
### Function
`z.iso.time(options?)`

### Description
Validates strings formatted as `HH:MM[:SS[.s+]]`. Seconds and sub-second decimals are optional by default. No timezone offsets or `Z` designators are permitted.

### Parameters
- **options** (object, optional)
  - **precision** (number, optional) - Constrains fractional second precision (`-1` for HH:MM, `0` for HH:MM:SS, `1` for deciseconds, `2` for centiseconds, `3` for milliseconds).

### Usage Example
```ts
const time = z.iso.time();
time.parse("03:15");              // Valid
time.parse("03:15:00");           // Valid
time.parse("03:15:00.9999999");   // Valid

const minuteTime = z.iso.time({ precision: -1 });
minuteTime.parse("03:15");        // Valid
```
```

--------------------------------

### Compile a Zod schema with z.compile

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/blog/introducing-z-compile.mdx

Compile an existing Zod schema into a flat, loop-free fast-path validator using z.compile().

```ts
import * as z from "zod";

const Player = z.object({
  username: z.string(),
  bio: z.string(),
  xp: z.number(),
  // ...20 more properties...
});

const CompiledPlayer = z.compile(Player);
```

### Invert a codec using z.invertCodec() in Zod Mini

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/codecs.mdx

Derive the reverse codec and invoke standalone z.decode() and z.encode() functions on the inverted schema.

```ts
const dateToString = z.invertCodec(stringToDate);

z.decode(dateToString, new Date("2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z"));
// => string

z.encode(dateToString, "2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z");
// => Date
```

### Validate numeric keys and numerical constraints in z.record

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Demonstrates validating numeric string keys and applying additional number constraints such as step, min, and max to record keys.

```ts
const numberKeys = z.record(z.number(), z.string());
numberKeys.parse({ 
  1: "one", // ✅
  2: "two", // ✅
  "1.5": "one", // ✅
  "-3": "two", // ✅
  abc: "one" // ❌
});

// further validation is also supported
const intKeys = z.record(z.int().step(1).min(0).max(10), z.string());
intKeys.parse({ 
  0: "zero", // ✅
  1: "one", // ✅
  2: "two", // ✅
  12: "twelve", // ❌
  abc: "one" // ❌
});
```

### Supporting Zod and Zod Mini with zod/v4/core

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/library-authors.mdx

Import from "zod/v4/core" in library code to access shared base interfaces, parsing utilities, and internal schema definitions.

```typescript
// library code
import * as z4 from "zod/v4/core";

export function acceptObjectSchema<T extends z4.$ZodObject>(schema: T){
  // parse data
  z4.parse(schema, { /* somedata */});
  // inspect internals
  schema._zod.def.shape;
}
```

### Constrain Set schema size with Zod methods

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Applies item count constraints to a Set schema using .nonempty(), .min(), .max(), and .size() methods.

```ts
z.set(z.string()).nonempty(); // must contain at least 1 item
z.set(z.string()).min(5); // must contain 5 or more items
z.set(z.string()).max(5); // must contain 5 or fewer items
z.set(z.string()).size(5); // must contain 5 items exactly
```

Add zod to devDependencies alongside peerDependencies to satisfy peer dependency requirements during library development.

```ts
// package.json
{
  "peerDependencies": {
    "zod": "^4.0.0"

  "devDependencies": {

  }
}

### Define and parse union schemas with z.union()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Checks the input against each option schema in order and returns the first value that successfully validates.

```ts
const stringOrNumber = z.union([z.string(), z.number()]);
// string | number

stringOrNumber.parse("foo"); // passes
stringOrNumber.parse(14); // passes
```
